clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy woman in her 40s presented with intense occipital headache and progressive lower limb weakness after receiving the AZD1222 vaccine. Initial brain MRI showed juxtacortical and deep subcortical white matter and corpus callosum lesions. She was treated with oral prednisone for 20 days, achieving complete remission. Two months later, after discontinuing prednisone, she experienced a severe relapse with progressive quadriplegia, loss of sensitivity with a C4 sensory level, and bladder/bowel involvement. Spinal cord MRI revealed longitudinally extensive signal alterations in the cervical and dorsal spinal cord (LETM). AQP4-IgG antibody testing was positive, while CSF analysis showed no alterations and negative oligoclonal bands. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of NMO AQP4+ was made. She received acute treatment with methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin, leading to improvement in motor and sensory functions at 3-month follow-up. Maintenance therapy with tocilizumab was initiated.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation with intense occipital headache and progressive lower limb weakness after AZD1222 vaccine.
Initial brain MRI showed lesions in juxtacortical and deep subcortical white matter and corpus callosum.
Initial treatment with oral prednisone 20mg daily for 20 days led to complete remission of symptoms.
Two months later, after discontinuation of oral prednisone, developed progressive quadriplegia, loss of sensitivity with a sensory level at C4, and bladder and bowel involvement.

Spinal cord MRI showed significant longitudinally extensive signal alterations in the cervical and dorsal spinal cord with increased thickness on T2 sequence, consistent with longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM).
AQP4-IgG antibody was positive by CBA.
CSF analysis showed no alterations and oligoclonal bands were negative.
Acute treatment for the severe relapse included methylprednisolone 1000 mg/day for 5 days, followed by intravenous immunoglobulin 400 mg/kg/day for 5 days.

At 3-month follow-up, the patient showed improvement in motor and sensory functions, with sensory level at T10 and recovery of upper extremity strength against gravity and trace muscle activation in the distal right lower extremity.
Maintenance therapy with the IL-6 inhibitor tocilizumab was initiated.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Negative oligoclonal bands in CSF, positive AQP4-IgG antibody, and presence of longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) are atypical for MS and strongly support NMO.
